prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, Members of the Committee,

I appear before this body today not to evade, but to clarify. I understand the gravity of the allegation that I departed the premises at the commencement of the fourth quarter with the intent to “beat traffic.” I recognize that in these uncertain times, such an action may be construed as subversive to the spirit of communal fellowship and tailgate solidarity.

However, I wish to state for the record: **I did not leave to beat traffic. I left because the potato salad had been sitting in the sun for three hours, and I feared for the gastrointestinal safety of this great nation.**

Let us examine the facts. At the start of the fourth quarter, the score was 38-3. The outcome was not in doubt. What *was* in doubt was the structural integrity of the deviled eggs and the ideological purity of a gathering where the host had switched to paper plates mid-event. Was my departure premature? Perhaps. Was it un-American? I submit to this Committee that there is nothing more patriotic than the responsible stewardship of perishable condiments.

Furthermore, I was not fleeing to the interstate. I was relocating to the shaded pavilion to establish a defensive perimeter around the remaining safe coleslaw. This was not abandonment; it was *containment*.

If protecting my fellow citizens from foodborne illness and preserving the sanctity of the post-game leftovers makes me suspicious in the eyes of this Committee, then I accept that burden. But I will not be branded a traffic-beater when I was, in truth, a mayo-saver.

I now respectfully yield my time, and would also like to yield the tongs, as I believe they have been cross-contaminated.
